messages:
anna: Ran an nsys capture on the slow tail of the 8k-batch run, attaching the timeline snippet I care about. There's a recurring ~40-80ms lull between device kernels where only host memcpy shows up.

samir: Can you paste the exact nsys command you used? curious if sampling or markers changed the behavior.

anna: used: `nsys profile -o /tmp/run1 --trace=cuda,osrt,alloc,cudnn --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-end=nvtx --stop-on-exit true python -m runtime.bench --cfg cfg/8k_batch.yaml`

kevin: thanks. two quick hypotheses: (1) host->device memcpy is happening on the app thread and getting preempted by linux scheduling, (2) KV prefetch is serializing and forcing a sync before the next kernel.

samir: I looked at the timeline: stream 3 shows `cudaMemcpyAsync (H2D)` as a tall block that sits between two kernels on stream 1/2. However stream concurrency is correct; kernels are not overlapping with that memcpy. CPU lane shows `sched` gaps aligned with the memcpy start times.

anna: exact mm: here's the timeline excerpt text i grabbed from the UI: ```
Time(ms)   Stream  Event
0          s1      conv_forward (kernel)  duration 12.4
12.4       s3      cudaMemcpyAsync H2D   duration 27.6
40.0       s1      matmul_gemm (kernel)  duration 8.9
48.9       s2      kv_prefetch (kernel?) duration 3.2
```

kevin: that pattern screams host-thread copy -> CPU preemption -> delayed kernel launch. If the memcpy uses pageable memory it will block the CPU syscall longer. Try forcing pinned pages with `cudaHostAlloc`/`cudaHostRegister` or change batcher to allocate pinned staging buffers.

samir: also noticed the batcher pads to multiples of 8 tokens for the GPU kernel selection heuristic. For small tails that padding doesn't pay off but triggers an extra prefetch step because we call prefetch for every padded sub-batch. Could be doing extra host copies.

anna: i can repro with smaller harness. Re-ran with pinned memory enabled and the lull shrinks from ~28ms to ~6ms. nvtx markers show memcpy latency drops accordingly.

kevin: good. two more things to try: (A) switch memcpy calls to a dedicated low-priority stream and let kernels on high-priority streams run, (B) change allocator so small tail prefetches go through an async zero-copy path (avoid extra staging copy).

samir: small note: the runtime's kernel selector chooses a different GEMM kernel for short sequences because it assumes contiguous batch layout; the selector probes by launching a tiny profiling kernel at model load. If that probe misclassifies some sequence shapes we get a slower kernel and more host work. worth validating the probe results in the model init logs.

anna: probe logs show we picked `gemm_f32_tiled_v3` vs `gemm_f32_unroll_v2` for tails. I'll force `unroll_v2` and re-run.

infra-bot: deploy-check: gpu nodes with kernel 525.85 and driver 535.x exhibit same traces — no known driver bug on record.

kevin: one more data point: run with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` to force deterministic ordering (only for debugging). If the gap disappears then it's definitely a scheduling/copy ordering issue rather than a kernel internal stall.

anna: did that, gap persisted but changed shape — blocking made the memcpy appear as shorter but the CPU sched gaps still line up. So pinned memory + dedicated memcpy stream was the fix in the repro.

samir: action items:
- anna: open a tiny PR to allocate pinned staging buffers for prefetch path when batch_size < 16 (so tails use pinned).
- kevin: add an opt-in runtime flag to route H2D copies to a low-prio DMA stream and test perf impact on throughput SLOs.
- anna: add a unit test to validate kernel selector probe consistency across tail shapes.

anna: i'll push the PR and link the nsys captures. thanks team :thumbsup:

kevin: nice find. this explains a lot of intermittent tail latency spikes we've been chasing in production.
